qs.q: A 32-year-old female presents with dysuria and frequency. Urine analysis confirms uncomplicated cystitis. Which medication should be avoided if she has a pre-existing reduced glomerular filtration rate?
qs.e: Nitrofurantoin is a first-line treatment for uncomplicated cystitis but must be avoided in patients with renal impairment due to reduced efficacy and increased toxicity. Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole and fosfomycin are alternative first-line agents.

qs.q: Which endocrine disorder causes an isovolaemic hyponatraemic state due to impaired water diuresis and reduced glomerular filtration rate?
qs.e: Hypothyroidism causes primary water gain resulting in an isovolaemic hyponatraemic state. Hyperthyroidism does not cause this specific defect in water diuresis.
